suggestions.title: Clear Credit card (sample) first
suggestions.text: It costs 7% a year, more than savings earn (3.5%), so paying extra off it is a guaranteed return. Car finance (sample) (6.9%) is next. Put a share of your leftover money into “Paying off debts faster” (most expensive first), or raise the monthly payment in Your figures.

suggestions.title: Emergency fund in place
suggestions.text: Your cash covers about 4.5 months of essential outgoings, meeting your 3-month target. Keep a small share going to it so it keeps up as your costs rise; anything beyond the target goes to your other choices.

suggestions.title: Higher-rate pension relief
suggestions.text: You pay 40% tax on your top slice of pay, so each £1 into your pension costs you only about 60p (claim the extra relief through self assessment if your scheme doesn’t give it). Salary sacrifice also saves National Insurance.

suggestions.title: Check for employer matching
suggestions.text: Your employer adds 3%. Many employers add more if you pay more — if yours does, that’s usually the best return available.

suggestions.title: Overpaying the mortgage beats cash savings
suggestions.text: Your mortgage costs 4.5% and cash earns 3.5%, so overpaying is a guaranteed saving once your emergency fund is in place. Investments are assumed to return 4.6% after fees but can fall. Most lenders allow 10% of the balance a year without a charge.

suggestions.title: Use your ISA allowance
suggestions.text: You have about £19,100 of this year’s £20,000 ISA allowance left. Growth and interest in an ISA are tax-free. For money you won’t need for at least five years, a stocks & shares ISA has historically beaten cash, but can fall in value.
